name: Unintended Proxy or Intermediary ('Confused Deputy')
principle: A component forwards a request or command to another sphere while dropping or replacing the original initiator identity. The target sees the intermediary's authority, allowing the requester to bypass access controls or hide activity.
detection_signals: Java URL.openStream()/URLConnection.openConnection() on req.getParameter() or other caller-controlled URL
Java HttpClient/Apache HttpClient execute(new HttpGet(userControlledUrl)) in a proxy/forwarder endpoint
C/C++ curl_easy_setopt(CURLOPT_URL, userControlledUrl) in a privileged service or backend relay
Forwarding code builds a new outbound request without propagating authenticated user/principal/delegation token
setuid/root daemon accepts IPC/socket commands and performs open(), connect(), ioctl(), or DMA configuration using process credentials
Proxy endpoint forwards caller-controlled host, port, path, method, body, or headers to internal/admin services
Absence of SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid/SCM_CREDENTIALS check before acting on local socket commands
negative_signals: Outbound target is selected only from a fixed allowlist mapping, not raw caller input
Forwarded request includes a server-generated signed caller identity or delegation token verified by the target
Target authorizes the original caller principal, not the proxy service account alone
Privileged helper checks peer credentials with SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid before performing the operation
Proxy strips caller-supplied identity headers and replaces them with authenticated server-generated identity
Forwarder rejects unexpected schemes, hosts, ports, methods, directives, and redirects before dispatch
false_defense_traps: Logging the original requester but not sending/verifying it at the target
Trusting caller-supplied X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded, X-User, or X-Principal headers
Checking only that the caller may use the proxy, not that the caller may access the target resource
Hostname/IP blacklist instead of strict allowlist and canonicalization
Preserving identity in one hop but dropping it on redirects or nested backend calls
verification_focus: Does the intermediary preserve and cause enforcement of the original initiator identity for every forwarded target, command, and resource?

consequence_chains.trigger: Intermediary uses its own authority for a caller-directed resource in another sphere
consequence_chains.consequence: Resource is exposed to an unauthorized requester

consequence_chains.trigger: Caller controls an outbound URL or network destination sent by the server
consequence_chains.consequence: Server-side request forgery reaches internal or protected services

patch_principle: Use strong mutual authentication between intermediary and target.
Propagate an immutable, server-generated initiator identity through every hop.
Authorize the original caller at the target or at the proxy before forwarding.
Allow only explicit targets, ports, methods, commands, and resources intended for delegation.
Run proxy/helper with least privilege and separate credentials per requester where possible.
